 The Hon'Ble Justice B.R.Madhusudhan Rao

Between:
1.Shindhaya Bhudevi and others
 ... Appellants - petitioners
 And
1.S.Shiva Rajanna and another
 ... Respondents - Respondents
 Judgment

1. This memorandum of Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the MV Act') assailing the award passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - cum - District Judge, Adilabad (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVOP.No.399 of 2008,
dated 06.09.2012.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - cum - District Judge, Adilabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Appellants are the petitioners and respondents are the respondents in the MVOP.
BRMR,J 3.
Learned counsel for the appellants - petitioners submits that respondent No.1 remained ex-parte before the Tribunal hence he is not a necessary party to the appeal.
4. Appellant No.1 - petitioner No.1 is the mother, appellant Nos.2 and 3 - petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the brothers of the deceased S.Srikanth.

5.1 Appellants - petitioners have filed claim petition under Section 166(1)(c) of the MV Act read with Rule 455 of APMV Rules, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum from the date of the accident till the date of realization against respondent Nos. 1 Shindhaya Bhudevi And 2 Ors vs S.Shiva Rajanna And Anr on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192997980/
1 and 2 jointly and severally on the death of S.Srikanth.

5.2 It is stated in the claim petition that on 12.04.2008 while S.Srikanth and other labours were going in a lorry bearing No.ATW-5299 for unloading the dung loaded therein, the driver of the lorry drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over the lorry, turned turtle and that the occupants have suffered injuries.
S.Srikanth died on the spot.

The deceased was aged about 20 years as on the date of the accident,
was working as a labourer and earning an amount of Rs.8,000/- per month.

On the complaint,
Sarangapur Police Station, has registered a case in Crime No.36 of 2008 against the driver of the lorry BRMR,J for the offence under Sections 304(A) and 337 of IPC and prayed to allow the OP.
6.1 Respondent No.1 remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.
6.2 Respondent No.2 filed counter and denied the manner in which the accident has taken place, the age and income of the deceased S.Srikanth.
It is further contended that the deceased might have been travelling as fare passenger but not as a labourer in the vehicle.

7. The learned Tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the pleaded accident occurred resulting in death of the deceased?
2. Whether the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent act on the part of R-1 or the driver of R-1's vehicle?
3.
Whether the vehicle of R-1 stood insured with R-2 insurance company on the date of the accident and if so, whether that policy covers the risk of the deceased?
4. Whether the claimants are entitled to compensation and if so, to what amount and what is the liability of R-1 and R-2?
5. To what relief?
8. Appellant No.1 is examined as PW1, examined PW2-K.Narayana and got marked Exs.A1 to A5.
On behalf of the respondent No.2 no witness is examined and no documents are marked.

9. The learned Tribunal after going though the evidence adduced by the appellants - petitioners with that of the documents marked thereon, BRMR,J has awarded an amount of Rs.3,48,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from 22.08.2008 till the date of deposit against the respondent No.1 and the claim against respondent No.2 is exonerated.

10. Learned counsel for the appellants-petitioners submits that the learned Tribunal erred in granting meager amount towards compensation against the claim of Rs.4,00,000/- and exonerating liability on respondent No.2.

The learned Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.ATW-5229 and the appellants - petitioners proved that the deceased died in the accident.

The learned Tribunal erred in awarding Rs.10,000/-
towards loss of estate and Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses, which are on lower side.

The learned Tribunal ought to have seen that the crime vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and Shindhaya Bhudevi And 2 Ors vs S.Shiva Rajanna And Anr on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192997980/
2 the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: Even though respondent No.2 did not adduce any evidence to rebut the evidence of the appellants - petitioners learned Tribunal erred in fixing the liability on the respondent No.1 alone.

Counsel to substantiate his contentions has relied on the decisions in the cases of (i) Sunita and others Vs.
United India Insurance Company Limited and Others 1 (ii) Tahera Bee @ 2025 LawSuit (SC) 964 BRMR,J Mohammed Taheera Bee and others Vs. APSRTC, Hyderabad and another 2 and prayed to allow the appeal.
11.

Sunita and others Vs.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company submits that the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded just compensation, rightly exonerated insurance company from its liability and no interference is called for.
The alternate argument of the counsel is that in case if the Court arrives at a conclusion that respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation, pay and recovery may be ordered.

12. Heard both sides, perused the material on record.
13.

Now the points for consideration are:
1) Whether the appellants - petitioners were awarded just compensation, if so?
2) Whether the award passed by the learned Tribunal suffers from any perversity or illegality, if so, does it require interference of this Court?

Point Nos.1 and 2:
14.

Appellants - petitioners have challenged the award passed by the learned Tribunal exonerating respondent No.2 - insurance company 2019 (4) ALD 505 (TS) BRMR,J from paying the compensation and also challenged the quantum in the appeal.

15. The learned Tribunal, while exonerating respondent No.2 from paying the compensation, has observed in the order as under:
"15- It is the contention of Petitioner that the said Lorry bearing No. ATW 5299 was insured with the second respondent.
Ex.A5 is the Xerox copy of the insurance policy over the said vehicle belonging to the first respondent Rajanna for the period from 25-4-2007 to 24-4-2008.
This accident took place on 12-4-2008.
Thus the Policy was in force by the date of accident.

But a perusal of Ex.A5 discloses that the coverage of risk for the owner and driver to a limit of Rs.2,00,000-00 was there, but there does not appear any coverage of the risk of any other employee working on the said lorry.
It covers the third party risk, third party property and a limited risk of owner and driver of the said Lorry.
Ex. A5 does not disclose payment of any premium for any labour working on the said Lorry.
The policy discloses that seating capacity including the driver was three and the net premium was paid to a tune of Rs.6,265/-.

Shindhaya Bhudevi And 2 Ors vs S.Shiva Rajanna And Anr on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192997980/
3 16- During cross-examination of PW-1, the second respondent contended that Ex.A5 policy does not cover the risk of any passenger or labour.

entities.text: Shindhaya Bhudevi And 2 Ors vs S.Shiva Rajanna And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Of course, the second respondent insurance company did not produce any copy of policy.

As there is specific suggestion to PW-1 that there was no payment of any premium for the coverage of risk to any of the employee of the said lorry and as Ex.A5 does not disclose payment of any additional premium to cover the risk of the employee, other than the driver of the said Lorry, it cannot, but be held that though there was insurance coverage for the Lorry, it does not cover the risk of the deceased.
This issue is accordingly answered."

16. Where commercial vehicle involved in accident is insured under liability - only policy excluding passengers, insurer remains liable to BRMR,J satisfy award under pay and recover principle despite policy breach, particularly when driver holds valid licence and vehicle weight witin permissible limit.

See: Sunita1.
17.

The insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident and the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from respondent No.1 - owner of the crime vehicle in view of the observation of the Supreme Court in Sunita1 case hence the learned Tribunal erred in exonerating respondent No.2 in paying the compensation, the same is liable to be set aside.

18. Insofar as the compensation is concerned learned Tribunal has taken the monthly income of the deceased Srikanth at Rs.3,000/- per month, arrived annual income at Rs.36,000/- (3,000 x 12),
deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses and the amount arrived is Rs.24,000/- per annum (36,000 - 1/3rd of 36,000), applied multiplier '14' and arrived at Rs.3,36,000/-, awarded Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses and in total awarded an amount of Rs.3,48,000/-.
19.

In Tahera Bee @ Mohammed Taheera Bee2, this Court has taken the income at the rate of Rs.8,000/- per month for a businessman who was doing scrap business basing on the Gazette issued by Government of India, Ministry of Labour and Employment, dated 31.05.2010.
BRMR,J 20.
Coming to the case on hand, accident took place on 12.04.2008 i.e., much prior to the Gazette dated 31.05.2010.

Appellants - petitioners stated in the claim petition that deceased Srikanth used to earn Rs.8,000/- per month and was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident, which is also the evidence of PW1.

This Court is of the view that if an amount of Rs.6,000/- is fixed towards income of the deceased S.Srikanth which will meet the ends of justice.
21.
The age of the deceased is taken as 20 years as mentioned in the claim petition.

Appellants - petitioners are entitled for future prospects, loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium as per the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi 3.
